description: Read one NET service order: its state, who must act next and what, the product's gates, and the verifiable service receipt that says exactly what has and has not happened (delivered, accepted, paid, settled, ecological outcome claimed). That read shows no party's wallet. A party to the order reads who the others are with their own signature: pass the order id and your wallet for the message to sign, then call again with the nonce and the signature (the buyer also gets the unsigned NET transfer of a live, accepted order there). The state read says whether the order is paid or a transfer of NET back to the buyer was recognized, and on what date; the payment and transfer-back transaction hashes and the quote and receipt hashes are shown only on the signed read, to the order's parties. A wallet that took an open task's provider seat reads only its own seat there until the buyer accepts it. Or pass a refusal code you were given and get its plain meaning and the next step. A dry-run order never shows a payment. Free, keyless for the state and signed by a party's own wallet for the parties, read-only, moves no money; it changes nothing about the order. Cost and signer: free; the state is keyless, the parties are read with a signature by a party's own wallet with no gas, and the house never holds a key.

nonce.description: With the signature: the nonce the message to sign carried (the time in milliseconds).

refusal.description: Optional: a refusal code such as insufficient_net_coverage; returns what it means and what to do.

signature.description: With the wallet and the nonce: the wallet's signature (EIP-191 personal_sign) of the message to sign.

wallet.description: Optional: your wallet, a party to this order (buyer, agent, provider or named judge), to read the parties with its own signature. Call with the order id and this wallet alone to get the message to sign.

name: net_order_status
title: Where a NET service order stands, and what a refusal means
